column1: How Do Metals and Non-Metals React?

column2: noble gases filled shell, they will show no reactivity
reaction of element is due to attainment of completely filled valency shell
the electronic configuration of noble gases & some metals & non-metals
Sodium atom has one electron in its outermost shell
If it loses that electron from its M shell then L shell now becomes the outermost shell & has eight electrons in its L shell
Sodium will now possess net +ve charge because it loses one electron giving rise to sodium cation Na+
Chlorine has 7 electrons in its outermost shell & it needs one more electron to complete its octet
If sodium & chlorine react, electrons lost by sodium would be taken up by chlorine
This gives sodium chlorine negative charge because number of e- & p+ in Cl are not equal
Thus we see chloride anion Cl-
Na -> Na+ + e-
Cl + e- -> Cl-
(chloride anion)
Note that sodium chloride does not exist as molecules but aggregates of oppositely charged ions
Na+ & Cl- are held together by strong electrostatic forces
Mg + Cl2 -> Mg2+ + 2Cl-
compounds formed in this manner by transfer of electrons from metal to non-metal are known as ionic compounds or electrovalent compounds
Ionic compounds are solids & are somewhat hard
These compounds are generally brittle & break into pieces when pressure is applied
the high melting & boiling points because considerable amount of energy is required to break the strong inter-ionic attraction
Electrovalent compounds are generally soluble in H2O insoluble in solvents like kerosene, petrol etc.
In solution or in molten compound in H2O electric current passes because ions move to opposite electrode when electricity is passed through solution
thus ionic compounds do conduct electricity in molten state

column1: Extracting Metals in Middle of Activity Series

column2: metals in middle of activity series like iron, zinc, lead, copper are moderately reactive
prior to reduction, the metal sulphides & carbonates must be converted into metal oxides
sulphide ores are converted into oxides by heating strongly in presence of excess air. This process is known as roasting
carbonate ores are changed into oxides by heating strongly in limited air. This process is known as calcination

ZnCO3(s) heat -> ZnO(s) + CO2(g)

ZnO(s) + C(s) -> Zn(s) + CO(g)
Manganese dioxide is heated with aluminium powder
3MnO2 + 4Al -> 3Mn + 2Al2O3 + Heat
reaction of iron(III) oxide (Fe2O3) with aluminium and the heat evolved. Molten iron is produced
Fe2O3 + 2Al -> 2Fe + Al2O3 + Heat

the electrical conductivity & melting point of an alloy are usually lower than that of pure metals
an example are alloys of copper & tin (bronze), and good conductors of electricity whereas copper is used for making electric circuits
